newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russia, U.S. could ease platinum crisis - Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: Russia, U.S. could ease platinum crisis - Dresdner.

text.p: The current supply squeeze on the platinum and palladium markets could be relieved if Russia resumed exports or if the U.S. were to sell strategic reserves, analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said on Friday.

"A rapid resumption of Russian exports would at least relieve the situation," Dresdner said in a report. Russian dealers are in Japan, and delivery dates have been named ranging from the end of next week to the beginning of July.
But such reports have been heard since April, without a sign of fresh supply, it said. Russia accounts for 25 percent of world platinum production, and 65 percent of palladium.
A supply squeeze in the physical market has sent platinum prices soaring to $500 an ounce from $400 on Monday.
The remaining straw to clutch at is the strategic metal reserves of the U.S. "Plans to sell these the year before last led to a sharp fall in prices in both metals," Dresdner said.

"Now would be a good time to use these reserves to push back the speculators who have caused the market massive damage. This could prevent even more serious damage, not just to the market, but to the world economy."

The recent sharp price rise threatens the many industries dependent on the two metals, including catalytic converters. Just-in-time production systems in the automobile parts industry leave the industry particularly vulnerable to such volatile price moves in the physical market.
